title: Predict: add or join?
idea: Read the quotes and the conversions, then predict whether a line adds numbers or joins text.

exercises.explanation: All numbers, so + adds every time: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
All text, so + joins every time: 222.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

print(int("2") + int("2") + int("2"))
exercises.explanation: int() turns each text into the number 2, so they add to 6.
Inside, 3 + 4 adds to 7 (numbers), then str(7) joins onto the label: Pts: 7. Math first, then convert to show.
No — text joins to 105. To get 15 you'd convert: int("10") + int("5").
Numbers add to 8 in the first two. The quoted/str versions join to 44.
int(x) is the number 6, times 2 is 12. Convert, then multiply.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

x = "6"
print(x + x)
exercises.explanation: x is text "6", so + joins: 66. No conversion was used, so no adding happened.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to its output.
exercises.explanation: Numbers add (2). Text joins (11). And math-then-str builds the message n = 2.

exercises.prompt: Before running any line, what one thing should you read to predict add-vs-join?
options: Whether the values are numbers or text (quotes? conversions?)
exercises.explanation: The TYPE of the values decides it. Spot quotes and int()/float()/str() calls, and you can predict the result.
